key_facts: conceived independently by two British naturalists, Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace, in the mid-19th century
All life on Earth—including humanity—shares a last universal common ancestor (LUCA), which lived approximately 3.5–3.8 billion years ago
The two-fold cost of sex was first described by John Maynard Smith
the earlier Permian–Triassic extinction event was even more severe, with approximately 96% of all marine species driven to extinction
Present-day extinction rates are 100–1000 times greater than the background rate and up to 30% of current species may be extinct by the mid 21st century

Defined by evolutionary biologist Ernst Mayr in 1942, the BSC states that "species are groups of actually or potentially interbreeding natural populations, which are reproductively isolated from other such groups."
Othniel C. Marsh, America's first palaeontologist, was the first to provide solid fossil evidence to support Darwin's theory of evolution by unearthing the ancestors of the modern horse
The Scopes trial decision of 1925 caused the subject to become very rare in American secondary biology textbooks for a generation
to be excluded once again in the 2005 Kitzmiller v. Dover Area School District case

forbidden_claims.claim: The Permian–Triassic extinction event wiped out about 42% of marine species.
Alfred Russel Wallace plagiarized his theory of natural selection from a manuscript Darwin sent him in 1858.
The Scopes trial permanently banned the teaching of evolution nationwide starting in 1925.

notes: Long Wikipedia article spanning mechanisms, history of life, and history of the idea; Darwin received Wallace's independent theory (not the reverse), a classic reversal trap.
